theory.intro: Here you work the other way round: given a description of how a quantity changes, draw the matching graph. A straight piece means a constant rate; a curved piece means a changing rate.
facts: When a container is filled at a constant rate, a **narrow** cross-section makes the height rise quickly (steep).
A **wide** cross-section makes the height rise slowly, so that part of the graph is shallow. A horizontal segment means the height stays unchanged.
A container with a **constant** cross-section, like a cylinder, gives a **straight** height-versus-time graph.
Each stage of a scenario becomes its own piece of the graph, joined in order at the time it ends.
A smooth change in behaviour is drawn as a smooth curve, not a sharp corner.
Refilling a tank takes time. Rapid refilling may appear as a steep rise at the chosen time scale, rather than an instantaneous height jump.
steps: Identify each stage of the scenario, in time order.
For each stage, decide whether the quantity increases, decreases, or stays constant.
For each stage, decide whether the rate is constant (straight) or changing (curved, and if so getting steeper or flatter).
Draw each stage as the matching straight or curved piece, joined in order, with axes labelled.

workedExamples.question_text: An empty spherical container is filled at a constant volume rate. Sketch the water-height–time graph from the bottom to the top of the spherical section. Explain how its steepness changes.

A cone-shaped container has a wide opening at the top and a point at the bottom. It is initially full. Water is removed through the bottom at a constant volume rate. Sketch the water-depth–time graph until the container is empty.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A cyclist travels at a steady speed, slows smoothly to take a bend without stopping, then smoothly returns to the original speed.
(b) A ball is thrown vertically upwards and caught at its release height. Measure height above the release level.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A digital service starts free. Its price rises quickly at first, then continues rising more slowly.
(b) A city's pollution level starts above zero and increases more and more quickly.

A cup of tea is initially at $85^\circ\mathrm{C}$. It cools quickly at first and then more slowly as it approaches room temperature, $23^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Sketch a temperature–time graph and mark both given temperatures.

Sketch a graph for each situation. Label the axes.
(a) A walker moves away from home at a constant speed, rests, then walks home at a slower constant speed. Show distance from home against time.
(b) A candle starts $18\mathrm{\,cm}$ tall and its height decreases at a constant rate until it is used up. Show its height during burning and afterwards.

A town initially has $1200$ residents and its population stays steady for a short time. After a new employer opens, the population increases slowly at first, then increasingly quickly. Growth later slows and the population finally remains constant. Sketch a population–time graph showing all four stages.

foundation.solution_text:
$A$ is correct.
The container has a constant cross-section, so the water height rises at a constant rate — a straight line.

$C$ is correct.
Near the bottom the container is narrow, so the height rises quickly at first; near the top it is wide, so the height rises more and more slowly — a curve that rises but gets flatter.

$B$ is correct.
The car slows down and speeds up smoothly through the corner, giving a smooth curved dip. Graph $A$ also has continuous speed, but its sharp minimum represents an abrupt change in acceleration. Graph $C$ shows instantaneous speed jumps.

$A$ is correct.
A jumping body follows smooth, rounded arcs under gravity, not sharp triangular peaks, so the graph should be made of smooth rounded humps rather than the sharp zigzags in $B$ and $C$.

development.solution_text:
$B$ is correct.
Near the bottom of the sphere the container is narrow, so the height rises quickly; in the middle it is widest, so the height rises most slowly; then as it narrows again near the top, the height speeds up again. This fast–slow–fast pattern gives a rising curve that starts steep, becomes shallow, then gets steep again — not the flat line in $A$ or the straight line in $C$.

Story 1 matches Graph $X$: the level stays constant, so the graph is a flat horizontal line above zero.
Story 2 matches Graph $Y$: the cost rises at a constant rate from zero, so the graph is a straight line starting at the origin.
Story 3 matches Graph $Z$: the wax burns down at a constant rate, giving a straight falling line, and then stays at zero once it is used up.

$C$ is correct.
The narrow bottom makes the height rise quickly at first. As the container widens, the same volume of water produces a smaller height increase, so the graph continues rising but becomes flatter.

mastery.solution_text:
$A$ is correct.
The lower section has a constant narrow cross-section, so the height first rises at a constant rate — a steep straight line. In the widening upper section, the height continues rising but more slowly, so the graph curves and becomes flatter. Graph $B$ ignores the widening section, and graph $C$ shows the height rising faster as the container widens.

$C$ is correct.
At first the water surface is in the wide upper section, so removing water lowers its height slowly. As the water level reaches narrower sections, the same volume removed produces a larger height drop. The graph falls slowly at first and then becomes steeper until the container is empty. Graph $A$ incorrectly shows a constant rate of height decrease, and graph $B$ reverses the change in that rate.
